name: arduino_bus
title: A library that carries I2C and SPI for drivers on Arduino
source: The Wire and SPI classes of arduino-esp32, in framework-arduinoespressif32 of PlatformIO

severity.high: with a working device and ordinary use of a public function, the program corrupts memory, hangs, returns wrong data or a false success, or the function cannot work at all. Data from a device counts as ordinary input whatever its length.
severity.medium: the same, but only after a fault (a dead device, a bus error), at a limit of a legal input from the application, or in a configuration the library offers and does not use by default.
severity.low: a leak on an error path, an unchecked call with no harm in ordinary use, a text that disagrees with the code.

i2c.text: carries I2C through a TwoWire object.

spi.text: carries SPI through an SPIClass object or by bit-banging.

esp_idf.text: compiles under ESP-IDF, on its own or with Arduino as a component. Note which.

nack_reported.text: a NACK or other failure of endTransmission() reaches the caller as a failure.

short_read_reported.text: a read compares what requestFrom() gave with what was asked.

large_transfers.text: a transfer longer than the buffer of the bus object is split or refused, and loses no byte in silence.

repeated_start.text: a write then read can keep the bus with no STOP between them.

speed.text: the clock speed asked for is applied, and a bus that cannot set it is reported.

probe.text: the presence check tells a device from an empty address.

transactions.text: beginTransaction() and endTransaction() are paired on every path.

chip_select.text: chip select is released on every path, errors included.

mode_and_order.text: mode, bit order and speed apply to hardware and bit-banged transfers alike.

bit_bang_timing.text: bit-banging keeps the clock at or under the speed asked for.

bounded_waits.text: every wait has an end, so a dead device cannot hang the program.

several_devices.text: two devices work in one program: no state of one lives in a global or static.

shared_bus.text: two devices share one bus, each with its own settings.

thread_safety.text: a lock or a stated rule for use from several tasks.

errors_returned.text: a failure reaches the caller as a value it can tell apart.

buffers_bounded.text: lengths are checked before they are copied into a buffer.

allocation_checked.text: where memory is allocated, a failed allocation is handled.

tests.text: tests that run without or with hardware.

docs.text: a README or API text that says how to use it.
